Rashi on Chagigah 5b:11:1.english: In the inner chambers - There is crying, as it is written: “In secret places” (Jeremiah 13:17).

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:12:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן ובבתי בראי ליכא והכתיב ויקרא - וכל קריאה השמעת קול היא:
Rashi on Chagigah 5b:12:1.english: So we read: "And in the outer chambers, there is none? But it is written, 'And [He] called'" - And every "calling" is a sounding of the voice.

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:16:1.hebrew: מאיגרא רם לבירא עמיקתא - כמה גדולה נפילה זו! אין לך גבוה ובור עמוק כמשמים לארץ:
Rashi on Chagigah 5b:16:1.english: From a high roof to a deep pit - How great is this fall! There is no [place] as high, and [no] pit as deep, as [the distance] from heaven to earth.

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:18:1.hebrew: תקפיה - רבי תקף לר' חייא, ואזיל רבי בהדיה:
Rashi on Chagigah 5b:18:1.english: He grabbed him - Rabbi grabbed Rabbi Chiyya, and Rabbi went with him:

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:18:2.hebrew: כי הוו מיפטרי מקמיה - שנטלו ממנו רשות:
Rashi on Chagigah 5b:18:2.english: When they were taking leave from before him - For they took permission from him [to depart].

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:18:3.hebrew: איכו השתא - אם לא באתי עמך והאמנתי לך, מנעתני מברכה זו:
Rashi on Chagigah 5b:18:3.english: Now, if - If I had not come with you and had believed you, you would have prevented me from this blessing.

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:19:1.hebrew: מנא לך - שכל כך גדולה הקבלת פנים:
Rashi on Chagigah 5b:19:1.english: From where do you [know this]? - That the receiving of [one's teacher's] countenance is so great.

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:1:1.hebrew: אינו מהן - מזרע ישראל, דכתיב "והסתרתי פני מהם" (דברים ל״א:י״ז), שצועק מצרות הבאות עליו ואינו נענה שלא יבואו:
Rashi on Chagigah 5b:1:1.english: He is not from them - I.e., from the seed of Israel, as it is written: "And I will hide My face from them" (Deuteronomy 31:17), for he cries out over the troubles that come upon him and is not answered, that they should not come.

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:1:2.hebrew: והיה לאכול - שהעובדי כוכבים שוללין ממונו:
Rashi on Chagigah 5b:1:2.english: “And they shall be devoured” - For the idolaters plunder his money.

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:1:3.english: And they seized him - They plundered him.

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:21:1.hebrew: היה רגיל כו' - מהלך שלשה חדשים היה מביתו לבית המדרש, ונוסע מביתו אחר הפסח, ולומד יום אחד, וחוזר לביתו לשמח את אשתו בחג הסוכות:
Rashi on Chagigah 5b:21:1.english: He was accustomed, etc. - It was a three-month journey from his home to the study hall. He would set out from his home after Passover, study for one day, and return to his home to gladden his wife on the festival of Sukkot.

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:2:1.hebrew: בחלום אדבר בו - "ביום ההוא" קא דייק: ביום, ולא בלילה, שמראין לו חלום כדי שיתפלל על הדבר:
Rashi on Chagigah 5b:2:1.english: “In a dream I speak with him” - [The verse says] “in that day,” which is precise: [it means] by day, and not at night, that they show him a dream so that he will pray about the matter.

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:2:2.english: His hand is outstretched - to protect him.

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:3:1.hebrew: אפיקורסים - שאינם מאמינים לדברי רז"ל, כגון צדוקים:
Rashi on Chagigah 5b:3:1.english: Epicureans [heretics] - Those who do not believe the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, such as the Sadducees.

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:3:2.hebrew: אחוי ליה - על ידי סימן רמז לו, החזיר פניו:
Rashi on Chagigah 5b:3:2.english: He gestured to him - By means of a sign, he hinted to him that [the Master] had turned His face [away].

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:4:1.english: With a gesture - By a hint.

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:5:1.hebrew: נסרחה חכמתם - באדום כתיב: ״האין עוד חכמה בתימן? אבדה עצה מבנים״ והכוונה מישראל:
Rashi on Chagigah 5b:5:1.english: Their wisdom has vanished - With regard to Edom it is written: “Is wisdom no more in Teiman? Has counsel perished from the prudent?” [This means] from Israel.

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:7:1.hebrew: שיחה יתירה - דברי שחוק שלפני תשמיש:
Rashi on Chagigah 5b:7:1.english: Frivolous speech - Words of levity before relations.

Rashi on Chagigah 5b:8:1.hebrew: כדלא טעים תבשילא - שרעב לאכול, כלומר, מתאוה לתשמיש:
Rashi on Chagigah 5b:8:1.english: Like one who has not tasted a cooked dish - For he is hungry to eat; that is, he craves marital relations.

Tosafot on Chagigah 5b:12:1.hebrew: הן אראלם צעקו חוצה - פשטיה דקרא בישעיה כתיב על המזבח, וכתיב: "הוי אריאל" (ישעיהו כט):
Tosafot on Chagigah 5b:12:1.english: "Behold, their valiant ones cry without" - The plain sense of the verse in Isaiah is that it is written about the altar, and it is written: "Woe to Ariel" (Isaiah 29).

Tosafot on Chagigah 5b:1:1.hebrew: שדור בי שבור מלכא וגרבוהו - אומר הר"י: דהיינו ההוא דבפרק בתרא דברכות (דף נו.) גבי פשריה דבר הדיא, שפתר לו שתמות אשתו ויאבד כל אשר לו מאת המלך:
Tosafot on Chagigah 5b:1:1.english: "Those of the house of King Shapur sent and plundered him" - The Rabbi Yitzchak says: This is the same incident as that in the last chapter of Berakhot (56a), concerning the interpretation of Bar Hedya, who interpreted for him [a dream, meaning] that his wife would die and that he would lose everything he had to the king:

Tosafot on Chagigah 5b:20:1.hebrew: ויחי עוד לנצח לא יראה השחת - פשטיה דקרא בתמיה הוא: וכי הרשע לא ימות כמו שהחכמים ימותו?!
Tosafot on Chagigah 5b:20:1.english: "That he should still live always, that he should not see the pit" - The plain meaning of the verse is as a rhetorical question: Will the wicked person not die, just as the Sages die?!
